A little perspective.
A clearer comparison.

Ferge compares two, three, or four text files at once. All loaded files stay visible. Choose a baseline to see how every other file differs.

Blocks
Corresponding regions line up across every file.
Fluid
Files keep their natural flow. Curves connect corresponding regions in neighboring panes.
Unified
Each comparison file interleaves baseline deletions and its own additions. The baseline stays visible.
+ Added− Deleted~ Changed

Text differences

The colored backgrounds on lines of text show additions, deletions, and edits. These differences are calculated against the baseline file. Uncolored text matches the baseline, subject to the Ignore whitespace setting. In Unified mode, an edit appears as a red old version and a green replacement.

Baseline and merge target

Baseline: the reference file chosen in the Baseline menu. Its file card and column marker identify that reference.

Merge target: the other file selected with the bullseye button or the Merge with menu. Its outline, tinted header, filled bullseye, and Merge target badge identify the file used by the copy controls. A file cannot be both the baseline and the merge target.

These file-selection markers are separate from the colored text backgrounds. Their colors come from the active theme palette. Selecting either file role does not edit its contents.

Copy a changed region

First select a changed region in a comparison pane. With A as the baseline and B as the merge target, Copy to baseline copies B’s selected region into A. Copy from baseline copies A’s region into B. Undo restores the previous file contents.

Drop files onto the shelf to add them; drop a single file onto a pane to replace it. Images and binary files are excluded. Automatic syntax detection can be overridden in each file’s language menu.

Clear all closes every file and leaves two empty drop panes. Closing either of the last two files also leaves an empty pane. Undo restores the files. Drop a file into an empty pane or use its Choose file button to get started.

Privacy and saving

Ferge compares files and pasted text entirely in your browser. It never sends your filenames, text, or edits to a server.

Saved in browser means your session is remembered in this browser. Imported files on disk are not updated automatically. Use Download file to save the current contents of any loaded file, including the baseline, with its filename.

Ctrl/⌘1–3: layout · Ctrl/⌘F: find · Alt+Up/Down: changes · Ctrl/⌘Z: undo
